# /crav1-design-architecture

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Design the architecture](../../from-design-architecture.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-design-architecture/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Work out an architecture change with the user, one decision at a time, in a sandbox until go-ahead.

[`/crav1-design-architecture`](crav1-design-architecture.md) (1.181.0, preview) decides how the landscape should change: systems and services and how they connect, environments, infrastructure and hosting, data flows, integrations, and deployment. It reads what the kit knows, shows two or three real options per decision with a reasoned recommendation first, folds in the user's own ideas as their own option, and records each settled choice as a draft ADR in a sandbox.

The sandbox is `docs/architecture/designs/<topic>/` on its own design branch: one goal per topic in `goal.md`, one or more designs under `designs/<name>/`, and `compare.md` once a topic fans out. The end state is designed first; staging happens only on `stage-it`, and the user names and divides the stages. A stage may wait on a stakeholder decision. No other skill reads the sandbox, even after it is merged.

The skill's `scripts/design_run.py` owns the folder format and every move, saves after each one, and refuses writes outside the topic folder before go-ahead. A run without the user may only prepare. At go-ahead the chosen design is reviewed, then copied as one block under `## Decided, not built yet` in `docs/architecture/spec.md` with a "Designed in" link, its draft ADRs are copied as accepted, and still-open questions go into that spec. The ending names pushing the design branch and opening its pull request first; planning comes only after that pull request is merged.

1.188.0: `change-goal` changes an open topic's goal in place: `design_run.py change-goal --topic <t> --input <json> --reason "<why>"` shows old and new without writing, then with `--yes` rewrites `goal.md` and logs the date, the reason and each change under `## Goal changes`. Decisions can be added, dropped, renamed or reordered; a dropped decision stays, marked `dropped` with its reason. A settled or leaning decision that is renamed, listed under `reopen`, or names a word from a removed constraint, criterion or driver is marked reopened for another look. A run without the user may not change a goal.

1.188.0: linked topics. `create --topic <t> --builds-on <base>` records `Builds on: <base>`, lists the base's settled decisions as fixed inputs, and cuts the design branch from `design/<base>` (updates by `git merge design/<base>`, never a rebase). `resume` names decisions the base settled or reopened since the last run, a local change of a base decision is refused with a `revisit` that reopens it in the base topic, `status` shows links both ways, and `go-ahead` on the linked topic waits until the base design is in the architecture spec on main, with a Waiting line naming the base pull request.

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which step | `resume` | Continue an open design topic at its first open decision. An optional topic value may follow. |
| Which step | `park` | Stop the current topic. It stays resumable. |
| Which step | `status` | Show open topics, designs, decisions, stages and questions. Writes nothing. |
| Which step | `fan-out` | Start a competing design under the same goal, as a copy or from a blank start. |
| Which step | `stage-it` | Suggest a split of the designed end state into stages that the user names and divides. |
| Which step | `go-ahead` | Review the chosen design, then copy it into the architecture spec after the findings are fixed or accepted. |
| Which step | `compare-topics` | One-off comparison of designs from different topics, with criteria the user picks. |
| Which step | `prepare` | Gather facts, draft options with recommendations, and refresh comparisons. Settles nothing. |
| Which step | `change-goal` | Change an open topic's goal in place after a card shows old and new, with a dated log; touched settled decisions get another look. |
| Which step | `builds-on` | Start a topic that builds on an existing one; the base topic's settled decisions are fixed inputs. |

Idea text with no word starts a new topic. A run without the user is always prepare, and with no word and no idea text it stops and names the words. Per-decision reply words: choose-a, choose-b, choose-c, choose-mine, discuss, add-my-idea, ask-me, to-question, to-research, skip-for-now.

## Runs when

You want to decide how the architecture should change. Called by the user. [`/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build`](crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build.md) may offer it.

## Prompts

One framing card for a new or changed goal, then one card per decision, plus at most 3 narrowing questions per decision when ask-me is picked. One decision per round. No cap on how many decisions a session may settle. A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: Architecture spec, system notes, environment docs, research, slice specs, code and config, and the topic's sandbox.

Reads `docs/architecture/spec.md` and `left-out.md`, `docs/system/` notes and ADRs, environment, infrastructure and hosting docs, research notes with their stale marks, slice specs when the ask touches one, saved data models when it touches data, code and config in the linked repos, and its own sandbox.

## Writes

In short: `docs/architecture/designs/<topic>/`; at go-ahead `docs/architecture/spec.md`, accepted ADRs, and the affected diagram.

Before go-ahead only `docs/architecture/designs/<topic>/` through `scripts/design_run.py`: `goal.md`, `compare.md`, and per design `design.md`, `questions.md`, `diagrams.md`, `adr/`, and `stages.md` once staged; a one-off file under `_compare/` only when asked. At go-ahead, after the review is fixed or accepted: one block under `## Decided, not built yet` and still-open questions in `docs/architecture/spec.md`, accepted ADR copies in `docs/system/adr/` or `docs/specs/<slug>/adr/`, and the affected diagram.

## Does not

Leaves `## Confirmed`, `## Accepted from a guess`, `## How the repos connect`, `left-out.md`, requirements, plans, tasks, verify, research notes, question mark lines, application code, pipelines, and live infrastructure alone. Does not commit, push, merge, tag, or open a pull request.

Limits and exceptions: A run without the user never settles a decision, stages, or gives go-ahead. A choice that reverses an accepted ADR, a constraint, or a current environment fact needs a separate yes. A requirement is routed to [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md).
